The sites reserved for high-rise residential have no official plans yet, so they start as a flat footprint. Slide up to 45 storeys to test a tall neighbour. The site reserved for a park stays open.

How this was made. Block and stack positions, unit types, storey ranges, sky-terrace pockets and the deck come from the HDB Rivervale Shores sales brochure (August 2017 BTO). Storeys are 2.8 m and the landscape deck sits on a one-storey carpark about 4 m up. Facade colours come from HDB photographs: dark warm-grey lower storeys, white upper storeys. Existing HDB blocks within 2.8 km come from the data.gov.sg building footprints joined to HDB Property Information storeys. Roads, the reservoir and parks beyond the plan come from the OneMap 2D map, aligned to those footprints. Heights of the child care centre, shops and non-HDB buildings are my approximations.

Stack facing is read off the site plan, and the dark/white colour split level is an estimate. Brochure notes say all surrounding forms and heights are subject to change. Treat the view and sun results as a guide and visit the site before booking.
